subs.name: Body and physical abilities
subs.q: Which abilities of my body do I want to keep or develop? What do I want to do more easily? What am I ready to rely on: assistive devices, guidance or my own sense of movement?

ЦС.situation: If I need to improve or heal myself, I trust one clinic: it picks the treatment, monitors it and reminds me when to come for a check-up.
ЦС.plus: Support for a specific function without having to master the whole technique; a clear contact for servicing.
ЦС.minus: Dependence on the quality of fitting, consumables and service; help from a device doesn't develop your own abilities.

practices.text: I go to a workshop where they fit my glasses and later repair them.

ЦЗ.situation: Twice a week I train with a coach who adjusts my load.
ЦЗ.plus: External motivation and timely feedback; a consistent sequence of sessions.
ЦЗ.minus: Cost and dependence on the coach's competence; an awkward schedule can get in the way of regularity.

practices.text: A coach builds a strength programme for me and corrects my technique.

ДС.situation: I choose my own watch or sensors for training and decide what to track.
ДС.plus: Support can be fitted to a personal goal and changed piece by piece; the chosen metrics are visible.
ДС.minus: Measurement and interpretation errors; costs of compatibility and maintenance; numbers can crowd out sensations.

practices.text: I compare data from my watch and app and adjust the load myself.

ДЗ.situation: I go to dance or movement classes to feel my body better.
ДЗ.plus: A finer sense of movement and independence in choosing a manageable load.
ДЗ.minus: Takes time and regularity; subjective sensation doesn't replace assessment of an injury or illness.

practices.text: I train my balance with yoga and physical exercise.

subs.name: Habits, sleep and recovery
subs.q: How do I want to feel after sleep and rest? Which rhythm of eating, activity and recovery suits me? How much daily attention am I ready to give it?

ЦС.situation: I use a ready-made sleep and nutrition programme with reminders.
ЦС.plus: Less daily planning; easier to repeat the chosen routine.
ЦС.minus: A ready routine may not match your life; without the programme the habit may not hold.

practices.text: I sleep and eat according to a sanatorium's fixed schedule.

ЦЗ.situation: With a sleep specialist I gradually change my habits and discuss the results.
ЦЗ.plus: Personal review of difficulties and gradual change; support for regularity.
ЦЗ.minus: Cost and meeting time; quality depends on the specialist's skill and how realistic the plan is.

practices.text: A sleep consultant helps me keep a diary and change my habits.

ДС.situation: At home, lights and notifications automatically switch to a calm evening mode.
ДС.plus: Fewer repeated decisions; conditions can be set to my own schedule.
ДС.minus: Settings need maintenance; not every device metric reflects the quality of recovery.

practices.text: I choose my own tracker, alarm and rest schedule.

ДЗ.situation: I watch when I get tired and adjust sleep and rest to how I feel.
ДЗ.plus: My own needs become clearer; the routine is easier to adjust when life changes.
ДЗ.minus: Observation takes time and can be inaccurate; persistent problems need separate attention.

practices.text: I go to bed guided by tiredness rather than a norm.

subs.name: Mental health
subs.q: What emotional stability and support do I want? What am I ready to change in how I relate to myself and my feelings? How do I want to get help in hard times?

ЦС.situation: I contact a service that matches me with a psychologist and arranges the session.
ЦС.plus: Easier to make the first step; fewer organisational tasks in a hard period.
ЦС.minus: Limited choice of specialists and formats; switching services can break continuity.

practices.text: I get a consultation through an accessible support system.

ЦЗ.situation: I meet a psychotherapist regularly and work through my reactions.
ЦЗ.plus: Stable contact and consistent work with feelings; personal feedback.
ЦЗ.minus: Cost, time and finding the right specialist; change can be slow.

practices.text: In a hard period I turn to a psychologist I know.

ДС.situation: I keep a journal and the contacts of people I can turn to for support on my phone.
ДС.plus: Support is collected in a convenient form; individual tools can be swapped.
ДС.minus: Needs setting up and judging quality; an app doesn't provide professional help on its own.

practices.text: I choose an app with exercises and decide myself when to open it.

ДЗ.situation: I write down what I feel and learn to understand why I react the way I do.
ДЗ.plus: More understanding of my own feelings and more say in choosing changes.
ДЗ.minus: You can get stuck in self-analysis or wrong explanations; it takes time and willingness to ask for help.

practices.text: I work through feelings by talking and writing.

subs.name: Cognitive health
subs.q: How do I want my attention, memory and clarity of thinking to be? What do I want to offload, and what do I want to keep as my own ability? How will I notice overload?

ЦС.situation: My calendar reminds me about medicines, bills and important meetings.
ЦС.plus: Fewer missed tasks and less load on memory; easy to start.
ЦС.minus: Dependence on the service being available; too many prompts can distract and hide changes in your state.

practices.text: I hand reminders and notes to a ready-made digital service.

ЦЗ.situation: When I have trouble with memory or attention, I see a specialist.
ЦЗ.plus: Difficulties are seen in the context of the person's state; there is professional feedback.
ЦЗ.minus: Limited availability and cost; not every plan transfers to everyday life as hoped.

practices.text: I train my memory with a teacher or mentor.

ДС.situation: I keep notes, decisions and my calendar in my own system where everything is easy to find.
ДС.plus: Needed information is easier to recover; the person sets the rules for access and reminders.
ДС.minus: The archive needs care; search errors or data loss create a new burden.

practices.text: I build a local assistant to search my own notes.

ДЗ.situation: Every day I read or think for an hour without my phone and notifications.
ДЗ.plus: Attention stays one's own support; fatigue is easier to notice.
ДЗ.minus: Results are hard to measure quickly; habits depend on life circumstances and don't explain every difficulty.

practices.text: I read complex texts and compare the arguments on my own.

subs.name: Prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and care
subs.q: How do I want to organise medical care and recovery? Who links my visits into one route? Which decisions do I want to take part in personally?

ЦС.situation: At the clinic a coordinator arranges my tests and collects the results.
ЦС.plus: Less organisational load; it's clear who is responsible for the next step.
ЦС.minus: Network and coverage limits; a standard route may handle an unusual case poorly.

practices.text: I book appointments and get prescriptions through a health service.

ЦЗ.situation: I see one family doctor who knows my history.
ЦЗ.plus: The doctor knows the history and circumstances; easier to link treatment with recovery.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on a particular team's availability; a risk of delaying a second opinion.

practices.text: For a long time I've been seeing one trusted doctor.

ДС.situation: I keep my test results and reports and decide myself whom to show them to.
ДС.plus: More freedom in choosing care; less history lost between institutions.
ДС.minus: Coordination stays with the person; information may be incomplete and prescriptions uncoordinated.

practices.text: I get my results myself and manage my records in an app.

ДЗ.situation: Before treatment I discuss different options with my doctor and how they would affect my life.
ДЗ.plus: Decisions are better tied to life priorities; the person understands the choice and its limits.
ДЗ.minus: Discussion takes time and energy; information can be complex and contradictory.

practices.text: I choose treatment together with my doctor after comparing benefits and risks.

subs.name: Income and inflows
subs.q: Where from and for what do I want to receive money? How far should income depend on time, results, capital or personal mastery? Which conditions suit me? Which inflows can I receive without working — help from others, benefits or money from selling property? Which are regular and which one-off?

ЦС.situation: I get a stable salary every month and don't look for clients.
ЦС.plus: Easier to plan inflows; no need to chase each payment.
ЦС.minus: Dependence on one employer; extra effort has limited link to income.

practices.text: I get a fixed salary for a permanent job.

ЦЗ.situation: I have a base salary and a bonus for my team's results.
ЦЗ.plus: Contribution and reward are linked; you can earn more inside the organisation.
ЦЗ.minus: Income fluctuates; criteria and assessment can change without the employee's say.

practices.text: My income grows with my manager's trust and the complexity of my assignments.

ДС.situation: I get income from my own flat or another asset, taking the costs into account.
ДС.plus: Part of the inflow doesn't require selling personal time for each payment.
ДС.minus: Requires capital; vacancies, losses, management costs and falling payouts are possible.

practices.text: I combine income from rent, a digital product and an asset portfolio.

ДЗ.situation: I sell my own course or product that I came up with and made myself.
ДЗ.plus: Reward is tied to quality and a personal professional signature.
ДЗ.minus: Income depends on demand, reputation and ability to work; scaling can change quality.

practices.text: I sell a product I made directly to clients.

subs.name: Spending and obligations
subs.q: How do I want to allocate current money and pay obligations? Which spending decisions do I keep for myself? How do I keep payments within my means?

ЦС.situation: My phone and utility bills are paid automatically.
ЦС.plus: Fewer forgotten bills and manual repetitions.
ЦС.minus: Mistakes can repeat automatically; it's easy to stop noticing regular costs growing.

practices.text: I set money aside for mandatory payments in envelopes.

ЦЗ.situation: Once a month I go through the family budget with a financial adviser.
ЦЗ.plus: Easier to make sense of complex spending and work out a realistic order.
ЦЗ.minus: The cost of advice; possible conflict of interest; the person still has to follow the plan.

practices.text: A financial adviser helps me sort out debts and spending.

ДС.situation: I set spending and payment limits in an app and review them.
ДС.plus: Routine payments follow my own rules; deviations are visible.
ДС.minus: Settings and balances need checking; an error in one rule can affect several payments.

practices.text: I record spending in a notebook by my own categories.

ДЗ.situation: My family and I decide together what to spend money on and what not to buy.
ДЗ.plus: Spending is tied to meaningful priorities; the cost of obligations is easier to see.
ДЗ.minus: Takes attention and conversations; people may judge what's necessary differently.

practices.text: I separate spending on what matters to me from purchases out of habit.

subs.name: Capital and savings
subs.q: What do I want to accumulate and why? Which assets and abilities do I consider my capital? From what means and for whom am I building it?

ЦС.situation: I put small sums aside and pay for big purchases in instalments.
ЦС.plus: You can keep your usual consumption and gradually build a reserve.
ЦС.minus: Capital grows more slowly; interest on loans can eat up savings.

practices.text: I put a small sum into the bank every month.

ЦЗ.situation: Following a plan with an adviser, I save for housing or education.
ЦЗ.plus: Capital is tied to clear life opportunities; easier to stay consistent.
ЦЗ.minus: Housing can be illiquid, education doesn't guarantee returns; the strategy needs revisiting.

practices.text: An adviser helps include inheritance questions in the family's financial plan.

ДС.situation: Every month I automatically top up my savings or investments.
ДС.plus: Regularity depends less on monthly effort; the choice of assets stays with you.
ДС.minus: Auto-saving doesn't remove market risk; a wrong initial choice is repeated too.

practices.text: I split my savings between deposits and diversified funds myself.

ДЗ.situation: In our family we discuss inheritance and teach the children how to handle money.
ДЗ.plus: Useful assets and experience can be kept for the long term; continuity grows stronger.
ДЗ.minus: Possible conflicts between heirs, concentration of wealth and limits on personal choice.

subs.name: Financial resilience
subs.q: What will I rely on if I lose income or face a big expense? For how long do I want to be prepared? Which obligations and dependencies am I ready to accept?

ЦС.situation: I know what help or insurance I can count on if I lose my job.
ЦС.plus: Less self-organised protection; existing programmes are used.
ЦС.minus: A short personal horizon; outside help can be limited or late, and credit creates debt.

practices.text: I keep some money for illness or job loss.

ЦЗ.situation: I plan a financial cushion with an adviser to match my obligations.
ЦЗ.plus: Protection is matched to specific deadlines and obligations.
ЦЗ.minus: The plan depends on the quality of its assumptions; a specialist's help doesn't remove responsibility for loans.

practices.text: I consult on risks to income, health and property.

ДС.situation: I keep a reserve for several months of living on an accessible account.
ДС.plus: More time to rebuild after losing income; your own limits of protection are visible.
ДС.minus: A reserve takes resources and discipline; the estimate may underrate how long hard times last.

practices.text: I build a cash reserve and insurance policies myself.

ДЗ.situation: We agreed in advance who will take care of the bills and documents if I can't.
ДЗ.plus: A long horizon and several supports; knowledge isn't concentrated in one person.
ДЗ.minus: Complex agreements and different interests across generations; family support isn't guaranteed.

subs.name: Direction, role and professional growth
subs.q: Who do I want to be at work? What do I count as progress: conditions, scope of responsibility, project value, product quality or recognition? How do I want to change, reduce or end my professional role, and do I want other work afterwards?

ЦС.situation: I work as a specialist with a good salary and a convenient schedule, without managing people.
ЦС.plus: A clear role and a way to improve conditions; you can stay a specialist.
ЦС.minus: The ceiling depends on how the organisation is built; higher pay may come with a hidden rise in workload.

practices.text: I choose an employer with transparent pay and conditions for growth.

ЦЗ.situation: I lead a large team and project and am responsible for people and the budget.
ЦЗ.plus: You can influence a large result and people's growth.
ЦЗ.minus: More responsibility for others' work, more conflicts and organisational load.

practices.text: I lead a team and am responsible for a complex project in the organisation.

ДС.situation: I choose my own clients and run several independent projects at once.
ДС.plus: Freedom to choose projects; the value of expertise grows without a mandatory career ladder.
ДС.minus: Uneven workload, the need to sell your work and keep up proof of quality.

practices.text: I build a portfolio of project roles instead of a single permanent position.

ДЗ.situation: For years I've been developing my own product and working under my own name.
ДЗ.plus: Building deep mastery and a personal signature.
ДЗ.minus: A slow path to recognition; a high bar of quality can limit speed and volume.

subs.name: Getting tasks done
subs.q: How do I want to produce a concrete work result? Which decisions am I ready to make myself? What do I do personally, and what do I hand to software, a template or another person?

ЦС.situation: I get clear tasks, do them by the instructions and pass difficult cases to my manager.
ЦС.plus: It's clear what to do and when a task is finished; less uncertainty.
ЦС.minus: Little influence on the idea; instructions may not cover a difficult case.

practices.text: I do the work by step-by-step instructions.

ЦЗ.situation: My manager explains the purpose of the project, and I'm responsible for the result of my part.
ЦЗ.plus: The value of the work is visible, and there is support in difficult cases.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on the quality of management; approvals can slow work down.

practices.text: My manager explains the purpose of the task and helps me fix mistakes.

ДС.situation: I remove repetitive work routine with templates and configured tools.
ДС.plus: Repetitive work takes less manual effort; you can change the rules yourself.
ДС.minus: An error scales with the process; checking and maintenance don't disappear.

practices.text: I set up automatic report generation from data.

ДЗ.situation: I work several days in a row without meetings to do a complex task well.
ДЗ.plus: The chance to deepen mastery and solve non-standard problems.
ДЗ.minus: High time costs; hard to promise an exact deadline for exploratory work.

subs.name: Time, place and working conditions
subs.q: Where, when and at what pace do I want to work? Which conditions do I need? How important are ready equipment, colleagues nearby, mobility or the chance to go deep?

ЦС.situation: I come to an office where the equipment, internet and workplace are already set up.
ЦС.plus: Ready equipment and less organisational hassle.
ЦС.minus: Tied to a place and schedule; comforts don't make up for an awkward schedule.

practices.text: I come to a dedicated office at a set time.

ЦЗ.situation: I work next to colleagues and learn from them as I go.
ЦЗ.plus: Quick discussion and a sense of common cause; access to colleagues' experience.
ЦЗ.minus: Noise, interruptions and the need to agree on when to be present.

practices.text: I go to the office for meetings, mentoring and sharing experience.

ДС.situation: I work from home and agree my availability hours with clients myself.
ДС.plus: Work can be fitted to life, and the place can change.
ДС.minus: Organising conditions falls on the person; the boundaries of working time can blur.

practices.text: I switch between a home office and a coworking space.

ДЗ.situation: I agree on meeting-free days and work in a quiet place.
ДЗ.plus: Conditions support attentive work and an individual rhythm.
ДЗ.minus: Needs space, discipline and agreements; not every profession allows this mode.

subs.name: Collaboration and management
subs.q: How do I want to work with others? Who distributes tasks and decides in disagreements? Who can change the rules of joint work, and how? How do we pass on experience, documentation and unfinished work, and who owns shared results?

ЦС.situation: In my team everyone has a clear role and the rules of work are understood.
ЦС.plus: Less uncertainty about duties and accepting results.
ЦС.minus: Formal metrics can encourage rivalry and hide mutual help.

practices.text: The team is managed by roles, metrics and scheduled meetings.

ЦЗ.situation: I work with a strong leader whom I trust to choose the direction.
ЦЗ.plus: Disputes are settled quickly, and there is one direction.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on one leader; disagreement can be hard to voice.

practices.text: The leader helps the team reconcile conflicting goals.

ДС.situation: I assemble a team of independent contractors for a project and agree on the result.
ДС.plus: A flexible line-up for the task and limited contractual obligations.
ДС.minus: Coordinating separate parts can be expensive; shared responsibility can be blurred.

practices.text: I assemble a project team with shared documents and transparent tasks.

ДЗ.situation: In our small team we distribute roles ourselves and revisit decisions.
ДЗ.plus: Participants influence the rules and can use different strengths.
ДЗ.minus: Discussions take time; without clear authority, decisions can stall.

practices.text: The team itself discusses what to improve after a project.

subs.name: Purpose, route and access to knowledge
subs.q: Why do I need knowledge? What do I want to understand myself, and where is an answer enough? Who chooses topics, sequence and sources?

ЦС.situation: When a specific task comes up, I find a short ready-made guide instead of long study.
ЦС.plus: Quick access to what you need without a full course.
ЦС.minus: Shallow understanding and dependence on the answer's quality; harder to spot a mistake.

practices.text: I listen to a lesson where the teacher explains the right solution.

ЦЗ.situation: I study a long programme with a teacher and learn the subject systematically.
ЦЗ.plus: Consistency and reliance on the experience of teachers and authors.
ЦЗ.minus: Someone else's programme may lag behind your needs; considerable time and cost.

practices.text: I take a long programme with a teacher and discussion of the material.

ДС.situation: I learn a new tool through short lessons right on my own project.
ДС.plus: Specific needs are met quickly; the route is easy to change.
ДС.minus: Fragmented knowledge; constantly chasing skills can crowd out fundamentals.

practices.text: I choose courses on different platforms and keep my own learning plan.

ДЗ.situation: I explore a topic that interests me through books and archives, without exams or a diploma.
ДЗ.plus: Depth and freedom to explore without immediate gain.
ДЗ.minus: It's unclear when you've studied enough; gaps and dead ends are possible.

practices.text: Instead of a fixed programme, I gather a circle of people for joint research.

subs.name: Practice and applying knowledge
subs.q: How will I turn familiarity with a topic into the ability to act? On which tasks will I try? What should work without the help I had before?

ЦС.situation: I learn a language with ready-made dialogues in an app and practise pronunciation.
ЦС.plus: Easy to start; mistakes show up quickly.
ЦС.minus: You can learn to follow the prompt without mastering the action yourself.

practices.text: I practise on standard tasks with automatic checking.

ЦЗ.situation: I learn a craft from a master and make a real object with their hints.
ЦЗ.plus: Execution mistakes are noticed quickly; practical experience builds up.
ЦЗ.minus: Quality depends on the master and on available tasks; possible dependence on one way of doing things.

practices.text: I practise a skill with regular feedback from a mentor.

ДС.situation: I create my own exercises to master a skill I need for work.
ДС.plus: Practice is tied to personal tasks; good solutions can be reused.
ДС.minus: You may train only on convenient cases and reinforce your own mistakes.

practices.text: I create my own practice cycle of tasks and self-checks.

ДЗ.situation: I try to build something I don't yet know how to make and learn from my mistakes.
ДЗ.plus: Develops the ability to act without ready instructions.
ДЗ.minus: Lots of trial and error; hard to estimate the time and completeness of learning in advance.

practices.text: I learn skills in my own project with a living result.

subs.name: Feedback and recognition
subs.q: How will I know what I've learned and what I can't do yet? Whose assessment matters? Why do I need confirmation: licensing, professional trust or recognition of my contribution?

ЦС.situation: I take an official exam to get the certificate I need for admission.
ЦС.plus: A clear document saves you from explaining your training every time.
ЦС.minus: Formal success doesn't guarantee skill; requirements and recognition can change.

practices.text: I get a school-leaving certificate after exams.

ЦЗ.situation: A teacher goes through my work and shows what to improve.
ЦЗ.plus: Strengths and gaps are visible in detail; professional trust builds up.
ЦЗ.minus: Subjectivity and dependence on the chosen tradition of assessment.

practices.text: A professional community assesses a specific project, not just a diploma.

ДС.situation: I build a portfolio of real projects and reviews to show my skills.
ДС.plus: You can show concrete achievements to different audiences.
ДС.minus: A portfolio needs updating; not every audience trusts the chosen evidence.

practices.text: I gather skill credentials from different courses into a digital profile.

ДЗ.situation: I publish my own research and improve it after critical reviews.
ДЗ.plus: Feedback concerns the substantive value of your own contribution.
ДЗ.minus: Recognition may come late or not at all; a competent audience is hard to find.

practices.text: I prove my qualification with published work and a project result.

subs.name: Closeness, agreements and life together
subs.q: Whom do I consider closest? Do I need partnership and a shared household? How much shared life, mutual support and independence do I want?

ЦС.situation: My partner and I live separately and agree on meetings and shared expenses in advance.
ЦС.plus: Clear expectations and less organisational friction.
ЦС.minus: Predictability can make it harder to discuss changed needs; services don't create mutuality.

practices.text: I see my relatives on family holidays.

ЦЗ.situation: We gather as a whole family for holidays and support each other in hard times.
ЦЗ.plus: Belonging and stable mutual obligations.
ЦЗ.minus: Pressure of expectations; personal wishes can get lost behind habitual roles.

practices.text: I keep up regular family rituals and make decisions around my loved ones.

ДС.situation: My partner and I have separate plans and space, and we choose our shared days ourselves.
ДС.plus: More personal space and a flexible format.
ДС.minus: Less spontaneous shared life; support in a hard moment has to be agreed separately.

practices.text: I build a distributed network of care and regular meetings while living in different countries.

ДЗ.situation: My loved ones and I invent our own family traditions and rules of communication.
ДЗ.plus: The format can reflect the participants and change with them.
ДЗ.minus: Takes conversations and emotional work; a common language may fail in a conflict.

practices.text: Together we agree on boundaries, responsibilities and time for each other.

subs.name: Raising and developing children
subs.q: Do I want parenthood, and what place should it have in my life? How am I ready to invest time, money and attention? What help do I want to rely on?

ЦС.situation: Kindergarten, after-school care and a nanny help me combine children, work and personal life.
ЦС.plus: Easier to combine parenthood with work and other parts of life.
ЦС.minus: High cost and dependence on available help; delegating doesn't remove parental responsibilities.

practices.text: I use clubs, after-school care and available family services.

ЦЗ.situation: I fit my work around the children and organise family days together with relatives.
ЦЗ.plus: There is an image of the desired family and support from relatives' experience.
ЦЗ.minus: Traditional expectations may differ from the child's needs or the adults' possibilities.

practices.text: Older relatives take part in raising the children.

ДС.situation: I put together the schedule of school, clubs and helpers for my child myself.
ДС.plus: Help can be flexibly fitted to the family and its parts changed.
ДС.minus: The parent remains the coordinator; separate helpers may not see the whole picture of the child.

practices.text: I coordinate the schedules of several helpers and clubs in one calendar.

ДЗ.situation: Together with my child we choose what to explore and learn at home.
ДЗ.plus: Close contact and the chance to follow the child's changing interests.
ДЗ.minus: Needs a lot of time and attention; adults find it hard to tolerate an uncertain result.

practices.text: We discuss rules with the children and take their opinion into account.

subs.name: Care and help for loved ones
subs.q: How do I want to help loved ones when they can't cope on their own? What do I take on, and whom do I trust with the rest? How will I get help myself? What help do I want to receive and give after the loss of a loved one, including organising a farewell and supporting those left behind?

ЦС.situation: A home help service visits an elderly relative on a schedule.
ЦС.plus: Help depends less on one relative being constantly present.
ЦС.minus: Cost and dependence on the service; unfamiliar workers may keep changing.

practices.text: I order regular visits from a home helper.

ЦЗ.situation: Relatives agree on days to help an elderly family member, and there is a regular helper.
ЦЗ.plus: Familiar people know the habits better and notice changes.
ЦЗ.minus: Relatives get overloaded and duties are shared unequally; the limits of help are hard to discuss.

practices.text: I invite a regular helper whom my relative trusts.

ДС.situation: After a relative's operation I arrange separate services, transport and meal delivery.
ДС.plus: Help is fitted more precisely to the case; parts can be changed.
ДС.minus: A heavy load on the organiser; gaps between providers remain their job.

practices.text: I coordinate doctors' and helpers' visits in a family calendar.

ДЗ.situation: My neighbours and I take turns helping someone who finds it hard to cope alone.
ДЗ.plus: Care takes into account the person's wishes and the possibilities of several participants.
ДЗ.minus: Help isn't always available on time; complex needs can exceed what the circle can do.

practices.text: We agree with friends and family on mutual help.

spheres.name: Place of living and public environment

subs.name: Place of living and mobility
subs.q: Where do I want to build everyday life, and how tied to a place do I want to be? How often do I want to and can I move around? What matters more: nearby services, belonging, the option to move, or a base of my own?

ЦС.situation: I live near the metro, shops and a doctor, so I rarely need a car.
ЦС.plus: Less time on the road and organising trips; owning a vehicle is optional.
ЦС.minus: Convenience depends on density of services, timetables and fares; not every need will be close by.

practices.text: I use public transport and city routes.

ЦЗ.situation: After moving, I get to know my neighbours through the library and local events.
ЦЗ.plus: Familiar routes and people; easier to build local knowledge and trust.
ЦЗ.minus: Changing place can be painful; local habits don't suit everyone.

practices.text: Together with the community I restore a meeting place to keep ties with the neighbourhood.

ДС.situation: I can move to another city for a few months while keeping my work and usual services.
ДС.plus: You can change place faster to suit tasks and circumstances.
ДС.minus: Moves take money and energy; harder to keep lasting local ties.

practices.text: I use several services for housing, transport and mobile work.

ДЗ.situation: There is a home place I return to with my children and pass on family stories to them.
ДЗ.plus: A place to return to and an accumulated connection with people and history.
ДЗ.minus: Keeping the connection takes time; the next generations' interests may differ.

subs.name: Infrastructure, rights and safety
subs.q: How do I want to get basic services and help when things fail? Who protects my interests? What can I really choose, prepare or decide within the existing rules? How will I get water, energy and connectivity — through a provider, my own equipment or together with others?

ЦС.situation: When something breaks at home, I call a service that organises the repair itself.
ЦС.plus: Less bureaucratic and organisational load.
ЦС.minus: A fee and dependence on the intermediary; they can't always influence the service's own timing.

practices.text: I submit an application at an office window and get a ticket number.

ЦЗ.situation: If there's a dispute over a service, I trust a lawyer to handle my case.
ЦЗ.plus: The solution takes circumstances into account; the consequences of actions are clearer.
ЦЗ.minus: Cost and finding a competent specialist; the result also depends on outside institutions.

ДС.situation: I keep backup internet and service contacts in case of outages.
ДС.plus: Less vulnerable to a single way of access; easier to act during a failure.
ДС.minus: Backups need checking and money; they don't replace public infrastructure.

practices.text: I keep my own archive of documents and track my applications.

ДЗ.situation: When there are utility problems, I study the rules and push for a solution together with my neighbours.
ДЗ.plus: Knowledge and the ability to act grow; joint efforts can strengthen a request.
ДЗ.minus: Takes time and skills; personal activity doesn't guarantee an institution will change its decision.

practices.text: I join neighbours to jointly monitor how a city outage is fixed.

subs.name: Nature and environmental quality
subs.q: How important are air, water, quiet and living nature to me? Which conditions do I consider enough? What am I ready to change in my life for the environment, and how do I account for my impact? What do I want to preserve and restore, even without direct benefit to myself?

ЦС.situation: I live in a building where the management company services ventilation and water filtration.
ЦС.plus: You can get comfort without rebuilding your whole urban lifestyle.
ЦС.minus: Protection covers a limited space; nice design can hide unsolved environmental problems.

practices.text: I live in a district with waste sorting and public transport.

ЦЗ.situation: Together with my neighbours I sort waste and clean up the shared area.
ЦЗ.plus: Easier to join a clear shared practice; less to organise from scratch.
ЦЗ.minus: Without support from those around the habit may fade; an accepted practice isn't always ecologically effective.

ДС.situation: At home I monitor air quality myself with a sensor and a purifier.
ДС.plus: You can improve available conditions by your own criteria.
ДС.minus: Technology doesn't remove all sources of pollution; false precision of readings and the cost of consumables.

practices.text: I choose devices to save energy and control the climate at home.

ДЗ.situation: I live closer to nature and look after my plot, even if the trip to the city is longer.
ДЗ.plus: Ecological requirements are built into the way of life itself.
ДЗ.minus: Fewer conveniences and possibly long trips; a natural setting doesn't guarantee cleanliness and safety.

practices.text: Together with my neighbours I create rules for sharing resources and repairs.

subs.name: Taking part in shared decisions
subs.q: Which shared issues do I want to decide? Do I believe I can have influence, and what powers do I really have? What do I delegate, and where am I ready to take part in choosing rules and priorities?

ЦС.situation: The building council decides on repairs, and I read its reports.
ЦС.plus: No need to discuss every decision all the time; there is a defined person in charge.
ЦС.minus: Representatives can drift away from participants' interests; monitoring also takes attention.

practices.text: I vote for a representative in municipal elections.

ЦЗ.situation: Through a trusted representative I take part in solving my neighbourhood's problems.
ЦЗ.plus: A shared voice can be stronger than separate requests; easier to agree a direction.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on the leader; the minority's view can get lost.

practices.text: I pass agreed wishes on to the district representative.

ДС.situation: I vote online on improving my courtyard and check the result.
ДС.plus: You can have targeted influence without constant participation in meetings.
ДС.minus: A narrow agenda and digital exclusion; voting doesn't replace understanding the consequences.

practices.text: I submit projects and vote on a city participation platform.

ДЗ.situation: Together with my neighbours I decide what to spend money on and how to arrange the courtyard.
ДЗ.plus: Participants influence how the problem is framed and what the solution is.
ДЗ.minus: High time costs; an active minority may decide more than the rest.

practices.text: I take part in allocating part of the local budget together with others.

subs.name: Housing and home setup
subs.q: What kind of home do I want: a flat or a house, its size, surroundings, equipment? Do I need ownership, or is access enough? Which cares of setting up a home am I ready to take on?

ЦС.situation: I live in a convenient modern flat with services and delivery nearby.
ЦС.plus: Ready conveniences and fewer worries about equipment; services are close by.
ЦС.minus: Standard solutions and the complex's rules; regular fees and dependence on management.

practices.text: I live in a complex with ready infrastructure and services.

ЦЗ.situation: I live in the city centre so I can walk to meetings and exhibitions.
ЦЗ.plus: Access to cultural events, architecture and meeting places.
ЦЗ.minus: Price, noise and the limits of old buildings; living in the geographic centre doesn't make it CE.

practices.text: I choose to live near people with shared values and traditions.

ДС.situation: I rent where it's convenient for me now and move easily.
ДС.plus: Housing is easier to change with circumstances; fewer lasting investments in setup.
ДС.minus: Uncertainty about renewals and rules; repeated moves and limited influence over the space.

practices.text: I use a modular layout and local automation of my home space.

ДЗ.situation: I live in a country house with a garden and a workshop and arrange my household myself.
ДЗ.plus: More space and more ways to arrange everyday life to suit you.
ДЗ.minus: Cares about the house and grounds, costs and long trips; possible isolation.

practices.text: Together with my family I design a space for different rhythms and shared activities.

subs.name: Household and home services
subs.q: Which household tasks do I want to do, and which not? Who cooks, cleans and looks after things? How do we share the load, and how much will I pay for freed-up time? How do I want to supply the home with food and household items: buy, grow, make or share?

ЦС.situation: I order food delivery, cleaning and laundry so I don't have to do them myself.
ЦС.plus: A significant part of the routine is handed over; you get a ready result.
ЦС.minus: Constant costs, providers' schedules and fluctuating quality.

ЦЗ.situation: We have regular household helpers who know the family's habits.
ЦЗ.plus: A familiar person takes tastes into account and notices needs without detailed instructions.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on a particular helper; trust, pay and clear boundaries of work are needed.

ДС.situation: A robot vacuum and other appliances do part of the housework on a schedule.
ДС.plus: Less repetitive manual work; the mode can be set to suit you.
ДС.minus: Cost of equipment, space, repairs and maintenance; machines don't do all the housework.

practices.text: I choose appliances and apps to automate household tasks.

ДЗ.situation: I cook Sunday dinner with pleasure, and we share the rest of the housework.
ДЗ.plus: The joy of household tasks is kept; the load can be shared meaningfully.
ДЗ.minus: Agreements need revisiting; one person's favourite task can create work for another.

practices.text: I keep some household tasks as time for being together.

subs.name: Clothing, personal items and grooming
subs.q: Which things and care do I need? What matters more: novelty, quality, exact fit or sufficiency? Where am I ready to dig into details, and what share of the budget will I allocate?

ЦС.situation: I buy pre-selected outfits and don't spend time searching.
ЦС.plus: Quick choice and the pleasure of novelty; fewer comparisons.
ЦС.minus: Unnecessary purchases, dependence on recommendations and rising repeat costs.

practices.text: I choose items through an online shop's recommendations and delivery.

ЦЗ.situation: I buy well-made things and repair them instead of replacing them often.
ЦЗ.plus: Less attention goes to shopping; predictable quality.
ЦЗ.minus: A habitual choice may stop fitting; the price of quality isn't always justified by durability.

practices.text: I buy shoes from a craftsman I know.

ДС.situation: A service picks purchases by my rules and budget when they're really needed.
ДС.plus: Less searching with an exact match to the request.
ДС.minus: You need to formulate requirements; the assistant may promote what's good for the seller, not for you.

practices.text: I compare reviews, prices and specs in several shops.

ДЗ.situation: I wear a few simple things but choose the ones I love with special care.
ДЗ.plus: Money and attention are focused on what really matters.
ДЗ.minus: Careful choosing takes time; a favourite category can also become an expensive collection.

practices.text: I buy second-hand and repair things.

subs.name: Leisure, travel and experiences
subs.q: What do I want from free time: a change of events, cultural experience, personal impressions or depth and quiet? Do I need to travel for that?

ЦС.situation: I buy ready-made tours and often choose new short trips.
ЦС.plus: Lots of new events with little preparation.
ЦС.minus: Costs and fatigue from intensity; less time to get to know a place deeply.

practices.text: I book a package trip with transport and hotel.

ЦЗ.situation: I travel with a small club and a guide who knows the place well.
ЦЗ.plus: Meaningful context and company; less need to build the route yourself.
ЦЗ.minus: The shared pace and programme may not suit you; strong dependence on the leader.

practices.text: I choose a small trip with a guide matched to my interests.

ДС.situation: I build my own travel route with digital assistants and choose alternative experiences.
ДС.plus: You can get the right impressions without necessarily travelling far.
ДС.minus: Preparation and choosing take attention; possible dependence on a platform and loss of access.

ДЗ.situation: I spend my holiday in one city, walking unhurriedly and getting to know the place deeply.
ДЗ.plus: More time for experiencing, attention and rest at your own pace.
ДЗ.minus: Less variety in the same time; quiet and long free time can be expensive.

practices.text: I choose a trip that involves local life and learning a craft.

subs.name: Digital services, data and security
subs.q: How do I want to use communications, accounts and digital services? What am I ready to share for convenience? Who stores the data and is responsible for settings, recovering access and protection? What should happen to my accounts and files after my death?

ЦС.situation: I keep photos, documents and chats in one cloud account.
ЦС.plus: Fewer settings; convenient access and ready ways to recover it.
ЦС.minus: Dependence on the platform and its rules; handing over data doesn't guarantee security.

practices.text: A platform links several services into one interface and account.

ЦЗ.situation: A specialist helps me protect the family's devices and accounts.
ЦЗ.plus: Individual review and a contact for help; less self-study.
ЦЗ.minus: Cost and trust in the specialist; their mistake or excessive access also creates risk.

ДС.situation: I keep the family archive myself and make backups without depending on a platform.
ДС.plus: More control over storage and the ability to switch providers.
ДС.minus: Administration and backups fall on the person; storing it yourself isn't the same as protecting it.

practices.text: I set up a password manager and personal cloud storage.

ДЗ.situation: I don't post my personal life online and agree on privacy with my loved ones.
ДЗ.plus: Less unnecessary information ends up with strangers.
ДЗ.minus: Some conveniences and public opportunities are unavailable; you can't fully control your footprint alone.

practices.text: I remove unnecessary apps and limit notifications.

subs.name: My role, values and meaning
subs.q: What do I live for, and what role do I give myself in the world? What do I want to receive, continue, discover, create or preserve? What will make me consider my life meaningful? What place do worldview, faith and spiritual practices have in my life?

ЦС.situation: I use conveniences and services without setting myself a public mission.
ЦС.plus: You can value everyday life without the duty of having a great mission.
ЦС.minus: A sense of a meaningful life can depend heavily on the availability of external goods.

ЦЗ.situation: I take part in a big public project with a shared goal and rules.
ЦЗ.plus: A sense of continuity and of personal effort linked to a larger result.
ЦЗ.minus: If the shared cause is in crisis, personal footing can shake; one's own and accepted values may conflict.

practices.text: I choose to take part in a big mission with a strong team.

ДС.situation: I try new tools to do what I couldn't do before.
ДС.plus: Many paths for trying things and expanding personal experience.
ДС.minus: Constantly searching for the next opportunity can get in the way of depth and finishing things.

practices.text: I master new possibilities through open technologies and practice.

ДЗ.situation: Together with the residents I collect and preserve the stories of my neighbourhood.
ДЗ.plus: A sense of significance is tied to something concrete you created or preserved.
ДЗ.minus: You can overload yourself with a mission; the value of a contribution doesn't always get outside confirmation.

practices.text: I create a product I consider useful beyond my own life.

subs.name: Comfort and attitude to consumption
subs.q: What does consumption give me: convenience, status, emotions or support for what matters? Where is enough for me? For what am I ready to spend more, or to skip a purchase?

ЦС.situation: I pay for ready household services so I spend less time organising.
ЦС.plus: Everyday inconveniences can be steadily reduced.
ЦС.minus: The level of "enough" can keep moving away, raising costs and dependence on income.

practices.text: I choose convenient delivery, appliances and familiar services.

ЦЗ.situation: I belong to a prestigious professional club and feel I belong to my circle.
ЦЗ.plus: Choices help express belonging and the desired position.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on outside judgement; overpaying for a symbol and having to maintain status.

practices.text: I invest in services and things that my circle recognises.

ДС.situation: Instead of new things I buy interesting trips and experiences.
ДС.plus: Money brings experiences without having to accumulate things.
ДС.minus: Novelty quickly becomes ordinary; spending on access can be hard to notice.

practices.text: I choose trips and hobbies to my own taste.

ДЗ.situation: I don't replace a working phone, but I put money and time into a favourite hobby.
ДЗ.plus: Fewer unnecessary purchases; more resources for what matters.
ДЗ.minus: Needs your own criterion of enough; possible conflicts with those around and expensive exceptions.

practices.text: I create consumption rules that free up time and attention.

subs.name: Relationships with people, friendship and communities
subs.q: What place do other people have in my life? Do I need company, belonging, shared interests, deep understanding or a mix? What am I ready to give to these relationships myself?

ЦС.situation: I go to an organised dinner or walk to meet people.
ЦС.plus: Easier to find company and start talking.
ЦС.minus: Ties may stay superficial; the organiser decides access and format.

practices.text: I meet people through city clubs and ready-made events.

ЦЗ.situation: I help run local community meetings and feel needed.
ЦЗ.plus: A sense of belonging and being needed; a familiar circle of mutual support.
ЦЗ.minus: The community's expectations can become excessive; hard to step out of a habitual role.

practices.text: I support the regular meetings of a stable community.

ДС.situation: I have different communities for books, travel and other interests.
ДС.plus: Different interests find their company; the intensity of contact can vary.
ДС.minus: Fragmented attention; few people see the whole person or notice their absence.

practices.text: I connect circles of friends with different interests myself.

ДЗ.situation: I often meet two close friends for long conversations.
ДЗ.plus: You can be understood without having to be the same; trust survives change.
ДЗ.minus: Such ties take time and mutual wish; they can't be secured by one-sided effort.

practices.text: Every week I meet a close friend with no agenda.

subs.name: Creativity and self-expression
subs.q: What do I want to express or create — even if it brings no money and nobody needs it? How do I want to bring my idea to life? Do I want to share what I've made, and on what terms?

ЦС.situation: I make a family photo album in a ready-made service and give it to my loved ones.
ЦС.plus: A personal result comes quickly without long mastering of technique.
ЦС.minus: Expressiveness is limited by the format; works can look alike.

practices.text: I make an illustration from ready elements in an editor.

ЦЗ.situation: For several years I've been studying singing with a teacher and performing at small concerts.
ЦЗ.plus: You can reach expressiveness by relying on a developed tradition and a master.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on the teacher's aesthetics; a personal idea may not fit the chosen approach.

practices.text: I learn drawing in an artist's studio.

ДС.situation: I invent a story and use software to make pictures and music for it.
ДС.plus: You can quickly realise ideas beyond the technique you've mastered.
ДС.minus: Much time goes into selecting; limits of platforms, rights and control over the result.

practices.text: I combine different creative tools to experiment with a new format.

ДЗ.situation: I write stories in my own style, without aiming for views and likes.
ДЗ.plus: Your own voice and a deep connection with the material gradually form.
ДЗ.minus: A long path and an uncertain result; there may be no outside recognition.

practices.text: I develop a recognisable authorial language and my own theme.

subs.name: Contribution and public action
subs.q: Beyond my personal life, what do I want to support or change — and what am I ready to do for it? Do I believe my contribution can change something? What exactly?

ЦС.situation: I regularly donate to a charity and read its reports.
ЦС.plus: You can support a solution without a separate organisational role.
ЦС.minus: Little influence on the approach; easy to miss the absence of results.

practices.text: I rely on municipal services and established rules.

ЦЗ.situation: I help a civic organisation and do my part of a shared project.
ЦЗ.plus: Scale and division of labour increase what a personal contribution can do.
ЦЗ.minus: Dependence on the organisation's goals and quality; its interests may diverge from those of the people it helps.

practices.text: I take part in an association I trust to represent our interests.

ДС.situation: I choose a help project myself and switch if I don't see results.
ДС.plus: A contribution can be made regular and its direction changed independently.
ДС.minus: Convenient regularity can keep ineffective support going; reliable information about results is needed.

practices.text: I use digital tools to organise my own campaign.

ДЗ.situation: Together with my neighbours I collect data about a dangerous crossing and push for change.
ДЗ.plus: The link between participation and concrete benefit is visible; the approach can change with the situation.
ДЗ.minus: A high personal load and limited scale; the result may depend on one initiator.

practices.text: I organise a shared initiative with people based on discussion.
